Action-RPG

Examples include:

  • The Lord of the Rings: War in the North (video)

  • Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning (video)

  • Dark Souls (video)

An Android port of Monster Hunter Freedom Unite has been removed from the store, and Shadowlands looks floaty and dull. Am I missing anything?

Top-down hack-and-slash

Somewhat similar games but with a top-down camera.

Examples include:

  • Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance (video)

  • Dungeon Siege III (video)

  • Diablo III (video)

I might get lucky with these as there seems to be a number of them on Android, but most seem to be designed as semi-MMOs and look like cheap shovelware. Any good ones?

First/third-person shooter

A good shooter with proper twin-stick controls would be great.

Racing

If that helps, I am completely enamored with Colin McRae 2.0 on ePSXe (video), and I have good memories of Need for Speed Shift (video). In other words, something casual but still demanding enough to be meaningful.

Sports

The Android versions of FIFA don't have controller support for some (necessarily fucktarded) reason. I do have to mention Virtua Tennis Challenge (video), a perfect example of what I am looking for: it looks great and plays just like the home versions.

Reminder that I need the games to be playable offline, and controller-compatible.

Etiquette says I should offer my own examples, but so far I have only ever been convinced by two games:

  • Virtua Tennis Challenge as mentioned above looks fantastic despite its low reqs, and plays just like the console / PC versions. A safe bet for anyone: I don't see non-soccer fans being interested in FIFA, but anyone can enjoy a tennis game regardless of how much they care about the real thing.

  • The Bard's Tale is a poor consolation prize for the lack of Norrath / Dark Alliance (same engine, same era). I'm not a big fan of humor games but it's still a nice fantasy romp.

Other full-featured games for Android are games I would rather play on PC but I'll namedrop them regardless for the curious:

  • Jade Empire
  • Star Wars Knight of the Old Republic
  • The Infinity Engine ports (Baldur's Gate, Icewind Dale, etc)
  • The Final Fantasy series

That's it. Is it as hopeless as it feels like? Considering how good a game can look on the averate potato smartphone, surely there is an Android market I am missing out on.
